newsitem.title: USA: NYS agency to re-enter debt market after 22 years.
newsitem.headline: NYS agency to re-enter debt market after 22 years.

text.p: The New York State Urban Development Corp, which had to be rescued by the state in 1975, plans to sell about $600 million of bonds around the week of October 7, a finance official said on Wednesday.
Joe Branca, chief financial officer for Empire State Development, said the sale could go as high as around $623 million, as that is the amount of outstanding issues that need to be refunded.
Empire State Development is the umbrella organization for several entities, including the Urban Development Corp, which last tapped the capital markets in 1974.
Branca, who noted that the deal's details still are being discussed, said he expected the agency to tap the debt markets during the week of October 7.
While it was possible the agency will opt to sell the debt towards the end of the week of September 30, he said he doubted that would happen.
PaineWebber Inc will lead the underwriting team that will sell the bonds through negotiation, aided by Merrill Lynch & Co and Bear Stearns Inc.
The new debt will be sold in two parts, with the first comprised of around $400 million of senior lien issues, which the agency expects to be rated AAA.

As much as $223 million of subordinate lien issues also will be sold. They are expected to be rated single-A, Branca said, explaining that they would be backed by the agency's cashflow, and not carry any credit enhancement or insurance.

Since it was bailed out by the state in the mid-1970s, the Urban Development Corp has sold debt backed by funds appropriated by the New York State legislature, but this will be the first time it has returned to the capital markets with its own issues.
The Urban Development Corp expects to save money with the refunding, on a present value basis, which includes extending the maturity of the debt by 11 years to 2026.
"It completely restructures the New York State Urban Development Corp (issues) and it's the first debt issuance since 1974 for the Urban Development Corp on its own," Branca said.
No estimate of how much the agency stands to save was immediately available, partly because this calculation depends on market conditions when the issues are sold.

And as key part of the restructuring, the state will no longer have a moral obligation to repay the debt if the risk of a default should develop. "We're looking to remove the moral obligation of the State of New York," Branca said.
